key_insight: PhySGA combines an agentic planner, a physics-aware critic, and simulator actions to make 3D object composition more generalizable and interactive across rigid, articulated, and deformable objects.
clinical_relevance: While not a clinical tool, better physics-grounded 3D assembly can improve medical simulation, robotic manipulation, and digital training environments used in healthcare workflows.
method: Assembly Agent handles global step planning and coarse geometric/kinematic alignment.
Critic Agent diagnoses simulator state using contact dynamics and performs fine-grained closed-loop corrections.
Action Routers and a Self-Evolving Skill Library turn plans into simulator actions and reuse successful trial-and-error experience.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments in Isaac Sim showing improvements in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality over existing methods.
watch_item: Results are simulator-based, so real-world transfer and robustness to simulation mismatch remain important implementation concerns.
paper_title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
